title: Priority routing: customer messaging + FAQ for 429s, overload protection, and retries
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
## Goal
Create customer-facing messaging + an FAQ for the Hosted API changes related to hot-route capacity protection (tier-aware quotas/rate limits, priority routing, and overload shedding). Primary focus is clarifying:
- What customers will see (esp. 429 behaviors + headers + reason codes)
- How to interpret 429s (quota vs overload vs concurrency)
- Recommended client-side retry/backoff patterns (including streaming)
- How enterprise “priority” works (what it does/doesn’t guarantee)

This ticket drives the customer narrative and exact copy that will be used in docs, support macros, and release notes. Technical sources of truth are the gateway + policy schema + docs PR.

## Audience
1) Self-serve + growth developers (PLG): “Why am I getting more 429s? What do I do?”
2) Enterprise customers / TAMs: “Will this protect my SLO during regional pressure? What are the rules?”
3) Support/CS: “How do we explain reason codes, and when do we escalate?”

## Customer-facing framing (approved)
**Preferred wording:** “Capacity protection for hot routes” / “overload protection”
**Avoid:** Promising “guaranteed priority” in a way that implies infinite capacity.

One-liner:
> We’ve added capacity protection to keep the platform stable during traffic spikes. During periods of high load, best-effort traffic may be rate-limited earlier and more predictably so higher-SLA routes and tiers remain reliable.

## What’s changing (customer-visible)
### 1) More consistent 429 responses
- 429 responses are now standardized across protected routes.
- 429s can represent either **quota/rate limit enforcement** or **overload protection** (controlled shedding/backpressure).

### 2) New/standard headers (docs copy)
Customers may see the following headers on 429s (exact names per gateway implementation; keep docs aligned with ENG-4922 + PR-27441):
- `Retry-After`: seconds until next retry (when available)
- `X-Redwood-Request-Id`: request correlation id (for support)
- `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit`: numeric limit for the evaluated window (when applicable)
- `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining`: remaining budget (when applicable)
- `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset`: unix timestamp or seconds until reset (when applicable)
- `X-Redwood-429-Reason`: stable reason code (see below)

Notes:
- Some headers may be omitted depending on which enforcement triggered (quota vs overload) and endpoint type.
- We should ensure any examples in docs match what gateway returns in practice.

### 3) Reason codes (customer-facing list)
We will document reason codes as *stable* and suitable for programmatic handling.

**Proposed/implemented reason codes** (confirm final list with Amara + Cole; this matches current gateway contract from ENG):
- `quota_exceeded`: customer/org exceeded allocated quota for the active window
- `rate_limited`: request rate exceeded (short window limiter)
- `concurrency_limited`: too many in-flight requests for this key/tenant/route group
- `overload_shed`: request rejected due to fleet/route pressure (admission control)
- `overload_backpressure`: temporary rejection while queues drain (expect Retry-After)

Docs guidance on semantics:
- `quota_exceeded` / `rate_limited` are “policy/account” constraints.
- `overload_*` are “system protection” constraints and may occur even if you are under your nominal quota, during fleet pressure.

## Recommended client behavior (copy for docs + FAQ)
### Backoff strategy (default)
- Respect `Retry-After` if present.
- Otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter:
  - base delay: 250–500ms
  - max delay: 10–30s (client dependent)
  - add full jitter (random 0..delay) to avoid thundering herd
- Cap total retries by request type:
  - interactive/user-facing: 2–3 retries max
  - background/batch: 5–8 retries max

### When NOT to retry
- If you receive `quota_exceeded` and you’ve already hit your known quota ceiling, retries will likely continue to fail until reset.
- If you receive repeated `overload_shed` without `Retry-After`, backoff more aggressively and/or reduce concurrency.

### Concurrency and request shaping
- Prefer limiting client concurrency per API key (especially for long context / long generation workloads).
- If you do burst traffic, ramp gradually (token buckets fill predictably; immediate step-functions increase shedding).

### Streaming behavior
FAQ entry (for streaming endpoints):
- A request can start streaming and then terminate early under overload protection.
- The client should handle:
  - a clean stream termination (finish reason indicating overload where available)
  - a transport-level disconnect (retryable in some cases)
- Guidance: if partial output is unacceptable, treat early termination as a failed request and retry with backoff.

## FAQ draft (for docs + release notes + support)
### Q: Why am I seeing more 429s?
A: We introduced capacity protection to prevent fleet-wide tail latency and 5xx spikes during traffic bursts. When the system is under pressure, we throttle earlier and more predictably, especially for best-effort traffic.

### Q: Does a 429 mean my account is out of quota?
A: Not always. Check `X-Redwood-429-Reason`. `quota_exceeded`/`rate_limited` indicate you hit an account policy limit; `overload_*` indicates temporary system protection.

### Q: What should I do when I get a 429?
A:
1) If `Retry-After` is present, wait that long.
2) Otherwise back off with exponential delay + jitter.
3) Reduce concurrency and smooth bursts.

### Q: I’m an enterprise customer—will I still see 429s?
A: Possibly, but enterprise tiers are prioritized and have protected budgets on designated routes. During fleet pressure, we will shed best-effort traffic first. In extreme conditions, enterprise traffic can still be rate-limited to preserve overall stability and meet route SLOs.

### Q: Can I request higher limits / burst allowances?
A: Yes. Contact Support/CS with:
- route(s)
- expected RPS + burst shape
- typical prompt + output token distribution
- region(s)
- desired SLO
We may grant exceptions with guardrails and monitoring.

### Q: How do I debug a 429 with Support?
A: Provide `X-Redwood-Request-Id`, timestamp, region, route, and the full response headers. Support will use reason code + dashboards to determine if it was quota vs overload protection.

## Deliverables
- Docs page updates (Wei/Elliot): 429 reason codes + retry guidance + headers list
- Release notes snippet (Product)
- Support macro text + escalation criteria (Dev Patel / Owen)
- Short enterprise email blurb linking to docs + “what to expect” (Rachel / Liam)

## Acceptance criteria
- Final FAQ text approved by Product + SRE (for correctness) + Support (for usability)
- Docs PR merged and aligned with gateway behavior in at least one canary region
- Support macro published (or ready) before GA enablement

## Open questions (resolved)
1) Should we say “priority routing” publicly? **Decision:** Use “capacity protection” for public docs; allow “priority tier” language in enterprise comms where contractually relevant.
2) Are reason codes stable? **Decision:** Yes, documented as stable; additions allowed, but existing codes will not change semantics.
3) Do we show tier limits in Console? **Decision:** Not in this milestone for public UI; internal operator views only (Console backend hooks).

## Updates / Comments
### 2025-12-12 (Nikhil)
Drafted FAQ skeleton + asked Wei to align language with new docs section. Need confirmation from Amara/Cole on header names and final reason code list.

### 2025-12-16 (Dev Patel - Support)
Support request: include a simple decision tree:
- `quota_exceeded` => wait for reset / request quota increase
- `rate_limited`/`concurrency_limited` => reduce concurrency + jitter
- `overload_*` => backoff + reduce concurrency; if enterprise and sustained, escalate

### 2025-12-19 (Rafael Mendes - SRE)
Please avoid implying overload is “rare”. We want customers to treat it as a normal, safe failure mode during spikes. Also: emphasize jitter to prevent synchronized retries.

### 2026-01-08 (Wei Chen - Docs)
Docs PR in progress. Need final recommended default backoff numbers. Proposal: base 500ms, cap 20s, max 5 retries for batch.

### 2026-01-10 (Nikhil)
Approved Wei’s suggested defaults; incorporated into FAQ and release note text. Sent to Elliot for final pass.

Merged docs copy into PR-2217 pending final header verification from gateway responses. Suggest adding note: some headers omitted under overload vs quota.

### 2026-01-21 (Amara Diallo - Eng)
Confirmed `X-Redwood-429-Reason` header and `Retry-After` usage in overload backpressure path. `X-Redwood-RateLimit-*` headers present on quota/rate limit path; overload path may omit them.

Final copy shipped with docs PR merge and support macro ready. Marking Done. Follow-up: once Console exposes public tier/limit visibility, update FAQ to include where to see current limits.
